name: LanDeng Incense Technique Database
description: Machine-readable definitions of Chinese botanical incense techniques — heating, pressing, blending, appreciation, and carrying methods. Extracted from the LanDeng (澜灯) incense encyclopedia; every fact is traceable to a source page, and unverified facts are marked unverified.

mainEntity.name: Indirect-Fire Incense
mainEntity.description: 隔火焚香 (gé huǒ fén xiāng, "incense across fire") — the classical method of heating incense without burning it: a hot charcoal buried in ash, with a thin plate (silver leaf or mica) on top carrying the material, which warms but does not combust.

additionalProperty.name: Period
additionalProperty.value: Song dynasty (classical); precursor of Japanese kōdō

additionalProperty.name: Equipment
additionalProperty.value: censer (香炉), ash (香灰), charcoal (香炭), silver leaf (银叶) / mica (云母) plate, chopsticks (香箸)

additionalProperty.name: Smoke level
additionalProperty.value: minimal / near-zero (lowest-particulate method in the tradition)

additionalProperty.name: Related
additionalProperty.value: kōdō (香道), electric incense heater (modern equivalent)

sources.title: 隔火焚香 (Indirect-Fire Incense): Scent, No Smoke

mainEntity.name: Seal Incense
mainEntity.description: 香篆 (xiāng zhuàn, also 打香篆 / 打香印 "stamping incense") — the practice of pressing incense powder into a carved pattern with a metal mold and lighting one end so the pattern burns in sequence, serving visual beauty and timekeeping.

additionalProperty.name: Type
additionalProperty.value: powder-pressing technique; also a timekeeping practice

additionalProperty.name: Equipment
additionalProperty.value: censer with ash, metal mold (香篆模 / 香印)

sources.title: 香篆 (Seal Incense): Powder Pressed Into Patterns

mainEntity.name: 合香 Blending
mainEntity.description: 合香 (hé xiāng, "compound incense") — the classical practice of composing a blend of multiple ingredients on the 君臣佐使 (chief–minister–assistant–guide) principle, the same structural logic as a Chinese herbal formula.

additionalProperty.name: Period
additionalProperty.value: classical (Song–Ming manuals: 香谱, 香乘)

additionalProperty.name: Materials
additionalProperty.value: woods, resins, spices, herbs/roots, florals/fruits, binders (honey, makko, musk)

additionalProperty.name: Smoke level
additionalProperty.value: varies by formed shape (stick, pill, powder)

additionalProperty.name: Related
additionalProperty.value: 君臣佐使 (chief–minister–assistant–guide), 香方 recipes

sources.title: The 合香 Blending System: Composed Like a Formula

mainEntity.name: Incense Appreciation
mainEntity.description: 品香 (pǐnxiāng) — incense appreciation; attending to a fragrant wood (chiefly agarwood) with the focused, sustained attention given to music, codified in Japanese kōdō as "listening" (聞香, monkō) to fragrance.

additionalProperty.name: Period
additionalProperty.value: codified in kōdō (Muromachi, c. 1336–1573); Chinese origin in Song 隔火焚香

additionalProperty.name: Materials
additionalProperty.value: agarwood (jinkō 沈香) chiefly; sandalwood (白檀) secondary

additionalProperty.name: Equipment
additionalProperty.value: kōdō tools (香道具): ash, charcoal, mica plate, chopsticks, ash press

additionalProperty.name: Related
additionalProperty.value: kōdō (香道), rikkoku gomi (六国五味), monkō (聞香)

sources.title: Japanese Incense & Kōdō (香道): The Art From China

mainEntity.name: Incense Ceremony
mainEntity.description: 香道 (xiāngdào, "the Way of Fragrance") — the ceremonial appreciation of incense as a cultivated art, counted among the refined pastimes (四般闲事) and formalized in Japan as kōdō alongside the tea ceremony and flower arranging.

additionalProperty.name: Type
additionalProperty.value: ceremonial art / practice (not a household habit)

additionalProperty.name: Equipment
additionalProperty.value: kōdō tools (香道具): ash, charcoal, mica plate, ash press, chopsticks

additionalProperty.name: Related
additionalProperty.value: 品香 (incense appreciation), kumikō (組香), genjikō (源氏香)

sources.title: Japanese Incense & Kōdō (香道): The Art From China

mainEntity.name: Pill Forming
mainEntity.description: 香丸 (xiāngwán) — the classical 合香 delivery technique of binding a compound blend with honey, rolling it into pellets, and (in some recipes) coating the outside and air-drying before burning.

additionalProperty.name: Period
additionalProperty.value: classical (合香 pellet form, e.g. 二苏旧局)

additionalProperty.name: Materials
additionalProperty.value: compound blend bound with honey; optional coat (e.g. jasmine)

additionalProperty.name: Equipment
additionalProperty.value: hand rolling; air-drying (unverified detail: no dedicated tool named)

additionalProperty.name: Related
additionalProperty.value: 合香 (hexiang-blending), 二苏旧局 recipe

sources.title: The 合香 Blending System: Composed Like a Formula

mainEntity.name: Scented Sachet
mainEntity.description: 香囊 (xiāngnáng) — a small cloth pouch of fragrant herbs worn or hung for their scent; a carrying/wearing tradition rather than a burned one, in which aromatic roots and leaves release fragrance by proximity.

additionalProperty.name: Materials
additionalProperty.value: aromatic roots and leaves (当归 angelica, 松针 pine needles, 青蒿 sweet wormwood, 细辛 asarum)

sources.title: Pine Needles (松针) — Green Conifer Note

mainEntity.name: Fumigation
mainEntity.description: 熏香 (xūnxiāng) — incense that is burned / fumigated, the basic combustion practice of burning aromatic material to scent a space.

mainEntity.name: Flower-Scenting
mainEntity.description: 花熏香 (huā xūn xiāng) — the flower-steaming / flower-scenting technique recorded in the Ming-dynasty 香乘, by which a blossom (e.g. 瑞香 Daphne) scents a material rather than being burned as incense in its own right.

additionalProperty.name: Period
additionalProperty.value: Ming dynasty (recorded in 香乘 / Xiang Cheng)

additionalProperty.name: Equipment
additionalProperty.value: steaming apparatus (unverified detail: process named, not tooled)

mainEntity.name: No-Flame Heating
mainEntity.description: 空熏 (kōngxūn) — no-flame heating: releasing aroma below combustion temperature, achieved today with an electric incense heater, the accessible modern equivalent of 隔火焚香.

additionalProperty.name: Period
additionalProperty.value: unverified (modern electric heater; classical principle of 隔火焚香)

additionalProperty.name: Equipment
additionalProperty.value: electric incense heater (modern equivalent of 隔火焚香)

sources.title: 隔火焚香 (Indirect-Fire Incense): Scent, No Smoke

mainEntity.name: Single-Material Appreciation
mainEntity.description: 单方 (dān fāng, "single formula") — appreciating a single material alone (a piece of agarwood, a stick of pure sandalwood); the art lies in the material's own quality and grading, via heating technique.

additionalProperty.name: Equipment
additionalProperty.value: heating (隔火焚香) for appreciation and grading

additionalProperty.name: Related
additionalProperty.value: 复方 (compound), 隔火焚香 (indirect-fire), grading

sources.title: The 合香 Blending System: Composed Like a Formula

mainEntity.name: Compound Formula
mainEntity.description: 复方 (fù fāng, "compound formula") — 合香 proper: multiple materials composed into a structured blend on the 君臣佐使 principle.

additionalProperty.name: Related
additionalProperty.value: 合香 (hexiang-blending), 单方 (single-material), 君臣佐使

sources.title: The 合香 Blending System: Composed Like a Formula
